continue_on_error.description: Flag that specifies whether execution should continue if the flow hook throws an exception. Set to true to continue execution. Set to false to stop execution if the flow hook throws an exception. Defaults to true.
continue_on_error.rationale: Controls whether API processing continues when the shared flow fails. Continuing execution could bypass security controls implemented by the shared flow.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the flow hook can be unintentionally deleted or removed from Terraform management, potentially removing security controls applied across the environment.

environment.description: The resource ID of the environment.
environment.rationale: Identifies the Apigee environment where the flow hook is attached, and the correct value is organisation-specific.

flow_hook_point.description: Where in the API call flow the flow hook is invoked. Must be one of PreProxyFlowHook, PostProxyFlowHook, PreTargetFlowHook, or PostTargetFlowHook.
flow_hook_point.rationale: Specifies the functional attachment point where the flow hook is invoked. It is an architectural routing decision rather than a security toggle or exposure control.

org_id.description: The Apigee Organization associated with the environment
org_id.rationale: Identifies the Apigee organisation and does not directly configure security behaviour.

sharedflow.description: Id of the Sharedflow attaching to a flowhook point.
sharedflow.rationale: References the name or identifier of another shared flow resource. Platform-level policies should not constrain resource references or assume they can validate the internal security logic of the referenced shared flow.
